Life insurance for veterans: VA coverage and private options

Veterans have choices most people do not: coverage through the VA, private coverage, or both. Which costs less depends on your age, your health, and how long you need it. We lay the options side by side.

Reviewed by Luay Sadqi, Licensed Agent · NPN 21370662 · Updated November 2026

Schedule an appointment Call (301) 615-8289

What the VA offers

The Department of Veterans Affairs runs several life insurance programs. The three most veterans ask about:

  • SGLI (Servicemembers' Group Life Insurance) is group term coverage of up to $500,000 while you serve.
  • VGLI (Veterans' Group Life Insurance) lets you keep term coverage after you separate, from $10,000 up to $500,000 depending on how much SGLI you carried. There is a deadline to apply after separation, and applying early can let you skip health questions. VGLI premiums are set by age band, so they rise as you get older.
  • VALife is guaranteed-acceptance whole life of up to $40,000, in $10,000 steps, for veterans age 80 or under with a service-connected disability rating. There are no health questions. Full coverage starts after a two-year waiting period.

Program rules and rates are set by the VA and can change. Check the details at VA.gov life insurance before you decide.

When private coverage is worth comparing

  • You are healthy. VGLI charges every veteran in an age band the same rate. A healthy veteran can often qualify for private term life at a lower locked-in price, especially past age 50.
  • You want a level premium. Private term locks the price for 10 to 30 years. VGLI steps up every five years.
  • You need more than $500,000. A mortgage, young children, or a business can call for more than the VA maximum.
  • You want permanent coverage beyond $40,000. Whole life or guaranteed universal life can cover what VALife does not.
  • You want coverage for a spouse. Spouse coverage under the VA programs ends or must be converted after separation.
When VA coverage is the better choice: If you have serious health conditions, VGLI inside its no-health-question window, or VALife if you have a service-connected rating, may be coverage you could not buy privately at any price. We will tell you when that is the case.

Final expense for veterans

VA burial benefits help, but they rarely cover the full cost of a funeral. Many veterans add a small final expense policy so their family is not left with the balance. It can sit alongside VALife.

Turning 65 with VA health care or TRICARE

Health coverage is a separate question from life insurance, and the rules for combining VA care or TRICARE For Life with Medicare are easy to get wrong. Start with our turning 65 guide and call us before you enroll in anything.

Common questions

Life Insurance for Veterans FAQ

Should I keep VGLI or switch to private life insurance?
It depends on your health and age. Healthy veterans often find private term life costs less over time because VGLI rates rise every five years. Veterans with health conditions are often better off keeping VGLI. We compare both.
What is VALife?
VALife is whole life insurance from the VA with guaranteed acceptance for veterans age 80 or under who have a service-connected disability rating. It offers up to $40,000 in $10,000 steps, with full coverage after a two-year waiting period.
Can I have VA life insurance and a private policy at the same time?
Yes. Many veterans keep VA coverage and add private term, whole life, or final expense coverage on top.
Is Honorbrook affiliated with the VA?
No. Honorbrook Insurance is an independent agency and is not connected with or endorsed by the Department of Veterans Affairs or any government agency.
